review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

6:1.sourceText: Ὅσοι εἰσὶν ὑπὸ ζυγὸν δοῦλοι, τοὺς ἰδίους δεσπότας πάσης τιμῆς ἀξίους ἡγείσθωσαν, ἵνα μὴ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἡ διδασκαλία βλασφημῆται.
6:1.targetText: As many as are servants under a yoke, let them reckon their own masters worthy of all honor, that evil may not be spoken of the Name of God and the teaching;

groups.note: The passive blaspheming predicate is expanded as evil may be spoken of the Name/teaching. The English evil/speaking/of pieces render that one predicate, not separate Greek evil or speaking words.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

6:2.sourceText: οἱ δὲ πιστοὺς ἔχοντες δεσπότας μὴ καταφρονείτωσαν, ὅτι ἀδελφοί εἰσιν, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον δουλευέτωσαν, ὅτι πιστοί εἰσιν καὶ ἀγαπητοὶ οἱ τῆς εὐεργεσίας ἀντιλαμβανόμενοι. Ταῦτα δίδασκε καὶ παρακάλει.
6:2.targetText: and those having believing masters, do not let them slight [them], because they are brothers, but rather let them serve, because they are steadfast and beloved, who are partaking of the benefit. Be teaching and exhorting these things;

groups.note: The actual masters object of having is also the understood object of the following do-not-slight command. English repeats these same masters as bracketed them; the actual noun identity supports both expressions without a second source pronoun.

The middle ἀντιλαμβάνομαι with a genitive of the thing can mean partake of; Thayer explicitly gives τῆς εὐεργεσίας at1Timothy6:2 for partaking of the benefit. This contextual sense differs from helping a person in other uses of the same verb.

6:3.sourceText: εἴ τις ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖ καὶ μὴ προσέρχεται ὑγιαίνουσιν λόγοις, τοῖς τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τῇ κατ’ εὐσέβειαν διδασκαλίᾳ,
6:3.targetText: if anyone be teaching otherwise, and does not consent to sound words—those of our Lord Jesus Christ—and to the teaching according to piety,

groups.note: The present finite compound ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖ, teaches differently/other doctrine, is rendered be teaching otherwise in this conditional construction; no separate other/doctrine Greek words are invented.
The verb προσέρχεται literally comes toward and here denotes accepting/assenting to the teaching, rendered does consent; this contextual sense retains the actual assent predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

6:4.sourceText: τετύφωται, μηδὲν ἐπιστάμενος, ἀλλὰ νοσῶν περὶ ζητήσεις καὶ λογομαχίας, ἐξ ὧν γίνεται φθόνος, ἔρις, βλασφημίαι, ὑπόνοιαι πονηραί,
6:4.targetText: he is proud, knowing nothing, but unhealthy about questions and word-striving, out of which come envy, strife, slanders, evil-surmisings,

6:5.sourceText: διαπαρατριβαὶ διεφθαρμένων ἀνθρώπων τὸν νοῦν καὶ ἀπεστερημένων τῆς ἀληθείας, νομιζόντων πορισμὸν εἶναι τὴν εὐσέβειαν.
6:5.targetText: wranglings of men wholly corrupted in mind, and destitute of the truth, supposing the piety to be gain; depart from such;

groups.note: The accusative mind marks the respect in which people are corrupted; English uses in mind, without a separate Greek in preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness sentence addition: LSV depart from such follows TR ἀφίστασο ἀπὸ τῶν τοιούτων; pinned N1904 ends with the piety-as-gain clause and has no corresponding words.

6:6.sourceText: ἔστιν δὲ πορισμὸς μέγας ἡ εὐσέβεια μετὰ αὐταρκείας·
6:6.targetText: but it is great gain—the piety with contentment;

6:7.sourceText: οὐδὲν γὰρ εἰσηνέγκαμεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον, ὅτι οὐδὲ ἐξενεγκεῖν τι δυνάμεθα·
6:7.targetText: for we brought nothing into the world—because neither are we able to carry out anything;

review.note: LSV because corresponds to pinned N1904 ὅτι. The longer TR has an additional evident/clear predicate, δῆλον, which LSV does not print here; no unwritten source clear word is added to either side.

6:8.sourceText: ἔχοντες δὲ διατροφὰς καὶ σκεπάσματα, τούτοις ἀρκεσθησόμεθα.
6:8.targetText: but having food and raiment—with these we will suffice ourselves;

groups.note: The future passive ἀρκεσθησόμεθα means we will be content/satisfied; LSV recasts the experience as we will suffice ourselves. The English reflexive belongs to that translation, not a separate written Greek reflexive pronoun.

6:9.sourceText: οἱ δὲ βουλόμενοι πλουτεῖν ἐμπίπτουσιν εἰς πειρασμὸν καὶ παγίδα καὶ ἐπιθυμίας πολλὰς ἀνοήτους καὶ βλαβεράς, αἵτινες βυθίζουσιν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους εἰς ὄλεθρον καὶ ἀπώλειαν.
6:9.targetText: and those intending to be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and many desires, foolish and hurtful, that sink men into ruin and destruction,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

6:10.sourceText: ῥίζα γὰρ πάντων τῶν κακῶν ἐστιν ἡ φιλαργυρία, ἧς τινες ὀρεγόμενοι ἀπεπλανήθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως καὶ ἑαυτοὺς περιέπειραν ὀδύναις πολλαῖς.
6:10.targetText: for the love of money is a root of all the evils, which certain [ones] longing for went astray from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows;

6:11.sourceText: Σὺ δέ, ὦ ἄνθρωπε Θεοῦ, ταῦτα φεῦγε· δίωκε δὲ δικαιοσύνην, εὐσέβειαν, πίστιν, ἀγάπην, ὑπομονήν, πραϋπαθίαν.
6:11.targetText: and you, O man of God, flee these things, and pursue righteousness, piety, faith, love, endurance, meekness.

groups.note: N1904 πραϋπαθίαν and the TR πραότητα are related mildness/meekness nouns; LSV meekness expresses this shared character quality without pretending their Greek spellings/lemmas are identical.

6:12.sourceText: ἀγωνίζου τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα τῆς πίστεως, ἐπιλαβοῦ τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς, εἰς ἣν ἐκλήθης καὶ ὡμολόγησας τὴν καλὴν ὁμολογίαν ἐνώπιον πολλῶν μαρτύρων.
6:12.targetText: Be striving the good strife of the faith; be laying hold on the continuous life to which you also were called, and did profess the right profession before many witnesses.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective addition: LSV you also were called follows extra TR καί before called; N1904 has only the later καί coordinating and did profess.

6:13.sourceText: παραγγέλλω ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ζωογονοῦντος τὰ πάντα καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ μαρτυρήσαντος ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πειλάτου τὴν καλὴν ὁμολογίαν,
6:13.targetText: I charge you, before God, who is making all things alive, and of Christ Jesus, who testified the right profession before Pontius Pilate,

groups.note: N1904 ζωογονοῦντος denotes giving/preserving life, rendered making alive. TR instead prints the related ζωοποιοῦντος. The actual life-imparting/preserving head is linked with this lexical-form difference explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness recipient addition: LSV I charge you follows TR σοι, absent from this pinned N1904 verse. The actual next-verse σε is the subject of keeping and is not exchanged with this charged-recipient occurrence.

6:14.sourceText: τηρῆσαί σε τὴν ἐντολὴν ἄσπιλον ἀνεπίλημπτον μέχρι τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
6:14.targetText: that you keep the command unspotted, unblameable, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,

groups.note: The keeping infinitive after I charge is recast as the finite complement that you keep; that expresses this complement construction, not an independent Greek conjunction.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

6:15.sourceText: ἣν καιροῖς ἰδίοις δείξει ὁ μακάριος καὶ μόνος Δυνάστης, ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ Κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων,
6:15.targetText: which He will show in His own times—the blessed and only sovereign, the King of the kings and Lord of the lords,

review.note: The substantive participles βασιλευόντων and κυριευόντων designate those reigning and exercising lordship; LSV renders the persons as kings/lords, retaining those actual ruling heads rather than inventing separate royal nouns.

6:16.sourceText: ὁ μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν, φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον, ὃν εἶδεν οὐδεὶς ἀνθρώπων οὐδὲ ἰδεῖν δύναται· ᾧ τιμὴ καὶ κράτος αἰώνιον· ἀμήν.
6:16.targetText: having immortality alone, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no one of men saw, nor is able to see, to whom [is] honor and perpetual might! Amen.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article introduces the having-immortality description; LSV proceeds directly with having without an independent who/article word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies in as the light-dwelling complement relation; Greek οἰκῶν directly takes the accusative light phrase without an in preposition.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

6:17.sourceText: Τοῖς πλουσίοις ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι παράγγελλε μὴ ὑψηλοφρονεῖν, μηδὲ ἠλπικέναι ἐπὶ πλούτου ἀδηλότητι, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ Θεῷ τῷ παρέχοντι ἡμῖν πάντα πλουσίως εἰς ἀπόλαυσιν,
6:17.targetText: Charge those rich in the present age not to be high-minded, nor to hope in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God, who is giving to us all things richly for enjoyment—

groups.note: The compound high-thinking infinitive ὑψηλοφρονεῖν means be high-minded/arrogant; English to be high-minded renders that single actual attitude predicate.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness modifier addition: LSV the living God follows the added TR living designation, ζῶντι with its article; pinned N1904 has God who gives without a living participle.

6:18.sourceText: ἀγαθοεργεῖν, πλουτεῖν ἐν ἔργοις καλοῖς, εὐμεταδότους εἶναι, κοινωνικούς,
6:18.targetText: to do good, to be rich in good works, to be ready to impart, willing to communicate,

review.note: The compound/adjectival generosity designations ready to impart and willing to communicate mean generous and sharing; their infinitive wording is the English rendering of those actual adjectives, not extra giving/speaking Greek verbs.

6:19.sourceText: ἀποθησαυρίζοντας ἑαυτοῖς θεμέλιον καλὸν εἰς τὸ μέλλον, ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται τῆς ὄντως ζωῆς.
6:19.targetText: treasuring up to themselves a right foundation for the time to come, that they may lay hold on [that which is] truly life.

groups.note: The substantive future/coming participle μέλλον is rendered time to come; time is the English expression of futurity, not a separate Greek χρόνος noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: The bracketed English relative/copula that which is describes truly life; the Greek article supplies the relative designation only and no finite copula is written. LSV truly agrees with N1904 ὄντως, unlike TR eternal/continuous αἰωνίου.

6:20.sourceText: Ὦ Τιμόθεε, τὴν παραθήκην φύλαξον, ἐκτρεπόμενος τὰς βεβήλους κενοφωνίας καὶ ἀντιθέσεις τῆς ψευδωνύμου γνώσεως,
6:20.targetText: O Timotheus, guard the thing entrusted, avoiding the profane vain-words and opposition of the falsely-named knowledge,

6:21.sourceText: ἥν τινες ἐπαγγελλόμενοι περὶ τὴν πίστιν ἠστόχησαν. Ἡ χάρις μεθ’ ὑμῶν.
6:21.targetText: which certain [ones] professing—swerved concerning the faith. The grace [is] with you! Amen.

groups.note: Pinned N1904 ὑμῶν is plural you, while the TR ending has singular σου; English you does not distinguish those numbers. The link preserves the actual pinned plural identity.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
LSV closing Amen follows TR ἀμήν; pinned N1904 ends with you and has no Amen token.
